answer: Camera sensor fingerprinting (PRNU) ties each agent to one physical phone. First, the operator photographs a random code shown on screen. Second, the verifier extracts the sensor's noise pattern, pixel flaws as personal as a scar, like one hot pixel glowing as a faint ember. Third, the ledger rejects any pattern that correlates above 0.9 with one already enrolled. Fourth, a new photo is due every 30 days. So 10,000 sybils need 10,000 real phones at about $60 used, or $600,000. Passing one camera off as a thousand is like holding a mirror over a river and calling each ripple a new face.
